About this program
Interdisciplinary Health, Doctor of Philosophy
Explore complex health challenges from multiple perspectives through NAU's Interdisciplinary Health PhD. Conduct original research that brings health and social sciences together to advance understanding and improve health and well-being.
Explore health from every angle
NAU's Interdisciplinary Health PhD prepares you to investigate complex health challenges that can't be understood through a single discipline. You'll explore the connections between individuals, communities, environments, and systems while developing advanced research skills to examine questions related to health equity, disability, and psychosocial health.
Working with faculty across disciplines, you'll learn to integrate theoretical and applied perspectives, design rigorous research, and translate findings into knowledge that can inform practice, programs, and policy. Through original scholarship and interdisciplinary collaboration, you'll develop the expertise to contribute new perspectives to health research and prepare for careers as a researcher, educator, or leader in academic, community, government, and healthcare settings.
Bring diverse perspectives together
Draw on faculty expertise from across the College of Health and Human Services and the College of Social and Behavioral Sciences, gaining access to perspectives that extend beyond a single field of study. You'll connect with faculty whose work spans health sciences, rehabilitation, nursing, psychology, anthropology, social work, sociology, geography, disability studies, and other health-related disciplines.
This collaborative environment allows you to build a doctoral experience around your research interests while drawing on the methods, theories, and expertise most relevant to your questions. Through interdisciplinary mentorship and collaboration, you'll develop a broader understanding of the factors that shape health and discover new ways to approach complex research challenges.
Pursue the questions that matter to you
Research is at the heart of the Interdisciplinary Health PhD. You'll work with faculty mentors to investigate complex health questions using perspectives and methods from across the health and social sciences, developing original research that contributes new knowledge and informs practice, programs, and policy.
Choose from three specializations - Disability, Health Equity, or Psychosocial Health - to focus your research around your interests and goals. You might explore how people with disabilities experience and access healthcare, how social and structural factors influence health, or how psychological, social, and cultural factors shape health and well-being. Through interdisciplinary collaboration and original scholarship, you'll develop the expertise to address health challenges from multiple perspectives.
Turn research into meaningful impact
Graduates are prepared for research, teaching, and leadership careers in universities, research institutes, healthcare organizations, government agencies, nonprofit organizations, and other settings focused on improving health and well-being. Your interdisciplinary training can prepare you to lead research teams, develop and evaluate health programs, contribute to policy and practice, and educate the next generation of health professionals and researchers.
Through original research, scholarly publications, and collaboration across disciplines, you'll build expertise in your area of specialization and establish a foundation for contributing new knowledge in health equity, disability, psychosocial health, and related fields.
Graduate contact
Have questions about the Interdisciplinary Health PhD? Whether you'd like to learn more about the curriculum, research opportunities, faculty mentorship, or career outcomes, contact ihphd@nau.edu for more information. Learn more about the Interdisciplinary Health PhD.
